summary: We created a short illustrated story deck for school-age space fans about hardware NASA left on the Moon and Mars. It follows the Apollo lunar rovers, Mars rovers like Spirit and Opportunity, and the Ingenuity helicopter, explaining why each was left behind, what science it made possible, and what it still teaches us. Simple language and a “mission memory” style make each machine feel like a character with a life story. The project addresses the challenge by turning technical mission history into an engaging narrative that introduces young learners to engineering, exploration, and planetary science.
details: What it does: tells the story of discarded NASA hardware in 7 slides, one machine per slide, in kid-friendly language. Benefit: it makes space history accessible and sparks curiosity about engineering. Tools: Google Slides, NASA public mission pages for facts, and an AI assistant (Claude) for drafting text. Creativity: each machine is presented as a character with a “life story” rather than a spec sheet. Factors considered: reading level for school-age students, accuracy, and keeping each slide short.
